maria_support: FYI customer (jessica_acme) rotated their API key in AWS Secrets Manager and then updated k8s — now getting 401 invalid_api_key. Pasting the repro and logs they gave.
jessica_acme: Ran this after rotation and updating k8s secret, getting 401. Error body: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}  Really urgent, production traffic failing.

jessica_acme: Repro steps (from our ops runbook):
1) Copied new secret value from AWS Secrets Manager (we used the console).
2) kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=API_KEY=\"sk_live_abC123456789\" -n prod
3) Deployment picks up secret, calls Redwood hosted API and immediately gets 401.

jessica_acme: Example curl we tried:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Api-Key \"sk_live_abC123456789\"" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

acme-audit-bot: SecretsManager PutSecretValue event: SecretId=prod/redwood/key, SecretString='\"sk_live_abC123456789\"' (copy pasted as JSON string)

deploy-bot: k8s secret updated: redwood-key (namespace=prod) by jessica_acme at 2024-10-12T14:22:30Z

rahul_support: Thanks — this looks like the classic "embedded quotes" issue. When the console "Copy as JSON" is used or when the secret value is wrapped in quotes, the quotes become part of the secret literal. Redwood sees the header value with the extra '"' characters so the key mismatch returns invalid_api_key.

rahul_support: Quick checks: can you show the raw header your service sends (server side) and the exact k8s secret value (masked is fine, but show surrounding chars)? Also can you try curling without the quotes to confirm: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_abC123456789" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

jessica_acme: I checked logs, our outbound header literally has the quotes. We updated the secret with the quotes included. Sorry — we copied the value from the AWS console JSON pane.

rahul_support: Fix options — replace the k8s secret with an unquoted value. Example:
```
# replace secret without embedded quotes (client-side dry-run -> apply)
kubectl create secret generic redwood-key \
  --from-literal=API_KEY=sk_live_abC123456789 \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# or create from stdin to avoid shell quoting gotchas:
printf '%s' "sk_live_abC123456789" | kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-file=API_KEY=/dev/stdin -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -
```

rahul_support: Also for AWS: prefer `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/redwood/key --query SecretString -r` which returns raw string, or copy the value from the console "Copy secret value" (not the JSON box).

jessica_acme: Applied fix, restarted pods. Confirmed curl now returns 200 and API calls succeed. Thank you!! :white_check_mark:

maria_support: Closing the loop — root cause was JSON quoting when copying secret from the console -> quotes got stored in k8s literal and our header included them. KB note: document both the `--from-literal` exact usage and the printf/from-file method to avoid accidental surrounding quotes.

rahul_support: I'll add a short KB entry and include a suggested bash snippet for safely rotating secrets.

maria_support: marking resolved.
